title: Sweden's Recovery Looks Better on Paper Than in People's Wallets · 31 Aug
keywords: Sweden, Swedish economy, GDP growth, Riksbank, inflation, cost of living, household finances, unemployment, Swedish election, economic recovery, economic messaging, EU small economies, polling, opposition, government
notes: Sweden's economy grew 1.6 percent in the second quarter of 2026, prompting the government to upgrade its full-year growth forecast to 2.5 percent. But official statistics are doing little to lift the mood of households still grappling with high unemployment and financial strain. With a general election approaching and polls favouring the opposition, the gap between macroeconomic data and lived experience has become the defining political battleground.
